Symmetric free-form coordinate search (N=201, mirror-symmetric heights, multiplicative perturbations) reached only 0.723584 (p0007), well below the asymmetric stochastic searches (0.82-0.84). Imposing symmetry on the profile is a real handicap; the best profiles found are asymmetric.

Higher R correlates with a flatter f*f top and a shifted peak: the best result (p0004, R=0.837) has 7.6%/25.0%/38.3% of f*f knots within 0.1%/1%/5% of max with peak at 0.334, versus the constant's 0.12%/1.02%/5.02% at 0.5. Flattening f*f (raising the 1% and 5% shares) while keeping ||f*f||_inf low is the operative lever.

Does increasing resolution help? p0004 used N=400 and scored highest (0.8370) while p0002 (N=48) scored 0.8237 and p0003 (N=80) 0.7879, but these differ in search method too. Worth testing: fix the best search and sweep N to see whether finer discretization reliably raises R, and whether the asymmetric multi-block/edge structure persists at large N.
